author: independent runtime/product review
scope: Bounded actual Core CLI proposal-history paging acceptance; no production deployment or research-speed claim

baseline.classification: source-specific behavioral blind spot under explicit new config/Bound prerequisite
baseline.details: 35 actual coordinator proposal outcomes are durable, but the unchanged pre-paging phase exposes only the first 32 and no proposal_page. Policy deliberately returns a normal Stop, CLI returns 0, then the actual-worker assertion fails 0 != 1. This is not an unknown API/import failure and not a full unmodified Git baseline.

cases.name: test_tail_exact_and_conflict_page_selects_then_once_executes_real_task
cases.behavior: 4 real ReadProposals pages -> SelectProposals two tail outcomes -> Execute the one normally admitted queued task. Once is not spent on reads. One transparent actual ingress call; zero reservation/attempt/decision rows during all read callbacks. Final real CPU TREE/ECHILD, confirmed effect, 22-byte artifact, SETTLED, 2s conservative charge.

cases.name: test_tail_conflict_drives_stop_without_retry_debit_or_worker
cases.behavior: The actual tail conflict outcome changes Policy to Stop with its specific reason. 35 original proposal rows unchanged, one durable Stop, no attempts, reservations, or workers.

cases.name: test_real_proposal_cursor_is_rejected_on_evidence_channel
cases.behavior: A genuine proposal continuation token is returned on ReadEvidence while an actual distinct evidence token exists. CLI75 and no new attempt/reservation/decision/worker; 33 existing metadata-only prefix rows unchanged.

cases.name: test_peer_write_before_read_proposals_refuses_stale_continuation
cases.behavior: A real second SQLite connection commits an ideas.title change inside the callback, then Policy returns the actual proposal token. Revision validation rejects CLI75 before recording a decision, reserving, claiming, or launching.

static_review.conclusion: Within this bounded interface, proposal outcome pages remain detached historical metadata, not current-source or execution grants. Explicit proposal_page_size keeps old v1 and old v2 behavior opt-in unchanged. The real product tests exercise both callback revision refusal and separate cursor channels; normal dispatch still traverses original native qualification.
static_review.not_claimed: No universal all-history performance bound, cross-invocation cursor persistence, source adoption, or scientific inference from a proposal outcome.

 c.row_factory=sqlite3.Row
 attempt=dict(c.execute('SELECT * FROM execution_attempts').fetchone()); reservation=dict(c.execute('SELECT * FROM cpu_action_reservations').fetchone()); artifact=json.loads(c.execute('SELECT record_json FROM research_artifacts').fetchone()[0]); decisions=c.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cpu_action_decisions').fetchone()[0]
 terminal=json.loads(attempt['terminal_json']); binding=json.loads(attempt['binding_json']); ref={k:attempt[k] for k in ('task_id','phase','attempt_id','generation')}
 assert attempt['state']=='TERMINAL' and terminal['outcome']=='completed'
 assert reservation['state']=='SETTLED' and json.loads(reservation['ref_json'])==ref

 assert terminal['process_tree']['event']=='TREE_CLOSED' and terminal['process_tree']['wait_proof']=='ECHILD_WALL'
 assert terminal['process_tree']['binding']==binding['supervision']
 assert artifact['producer']==ref and terminal['artifact_ids']==[artifact['artifact_id']]
 raw=Path(artifact['path']).read_bytes(); assert raw==b'proposal tail observed' and hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()==artifact['content_sha256']
 effect=p/'results'/attempt['task_id']/'_execution_effects'/attempt['attempt_id']; prepared=(effect/'prepared.json').read_bytes(); committed=json.loads((effect/'committed.json').read_bytes())
 assert hashlib.sha256(prepared).hexdigest()==terminal['effect_receipt_sha256']
 assert committed['prepared_sha256']==terminal['effect_receipt_sha256'] and {k:committed[k] for k in ref}==ref and committed['event']=='effect_committed'
 assert decisions==0
summary['positive_durable_proof']={'ref':ref,'tree':'TREE_CLOSED','wait':'ECHILD_WALL','effect_receipt_sha256':terminal['effect_receipt_sha256'],'reservation_state':reservation['state'],'charged_nanoseconds':json.loads(reservation['permit_json'])['reserved_nanoseconds'],'artifact_sha256':artifact['content_sha256'],'artifact_bytes':len(raw),'normal_decision_rows':decisions}
test=repo/'tests/test_cpu_proposal_paging_product_review.py'; tree=ast.parse(test.read_bytes()); summary['test']={'sha256':sha(test),'functions':sum(isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name.startswith('test_') for n in tree.body),'asserts':sum(isinstance(n,ast.Assert) for n in ast.walk(tree))}
old=subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only','94dd2f7e2e30e31fe4a1740906abb7add5bf4bae','--','tests'],cwd=repo,text=True); assert old==''; summary['old_tracked_tests_changed']=[]
print(json.dumps(summary,sort_keys=True))

limits: Tests use the actual public CLI, original Orze/Lake loop and native Linux supervisor in new private temporary projects, but each CLI call occurs in the pytest interpreter rather than a fresh exec.

35 true proposal outcomes per project are admissions/exact replays/conflicts, not 35 workers. Only one candidate test launches one actual worker. The cross-channel case separately creates 33 metadata-only execution/effect fixtures, explicitly not native TREE proof.

Only the eight listed production modules plus the owned new test were frozen across each actual bounded run. Full-suite and entire-source freeze verification belong to the parent; they are not inferred here.
No existing test was modified; literal Assert counts are inventory, not proof of behavior by themselves.

Original baseline and candidate source/test snapshots, stdout/stderr, JUnit, complete generated project DB/files and report bytes are archived. Private account/license material and private Pro implementation are not included.
System test imports emitted the installed public Pro stub notice on the failing baseline; no actual Pro license was read or patched, and GPU/Pro lookup paths in the CPU fixture are fail-fast spies.
The historical outcomes do not lock a future Domain implementation or bypass current source/claim/permit/GO checks; normal admitted execution remains authoritative.
